identity.title: Widespread Molecular Outflows in the Infrared Dark Cloud G28.37+0.07: Indications of Orthogonal Outflow-filament Alignment

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present ALMA CO(2-1) observations toward a massive infrared dark cloud G28.37+0.07.

evidence.quote: IRDC G28.37+0.07[^1] (hereafter G28) is a massive (10$^5$ M$_\odot$) IRDC at a distance of 5 kpc.

question.value: Are CO outflows in IRDC G28.37+0.07 preferentially oriented relative to their parent filaments (and in a preferred plane-of-sky direction)?

evidence.quote: We can therefore compare the position angle between outflows and filaments, both easily observable in large-scale maps of clouds, to search for evidence of the accretion-filament correlation.

findings_qualitative.value: Outflow position angles peak near 100 deg (east-west); outflows appear mostly perpendicular to parent filaments in 3D.

evidence.quote: the distribution of the plane-of-sky outflow position angles peaks at about 100$^\circ$

claims.experiment: AD test of PA_Out against uniform
claims.finding: Outflow orientations are not random; east-west preference

evidence.quote: The p-value of the AD test is 0.15, indicating PA$_{\rm Out}$ is unlikely drawn from a uniform distribution.

claims.hypothesis: Outflows are parallel, random or perpendicular to filaments in 3D
claims.experiment: Monte Carlo projection and two-sample AD tests
claims.finding: Outflows mostly perpendicular to parent filaments

evidence.quote: Given our results we conclude that it is more likely that in G28 outflows are perpendicular to their parent filament

limitations_admitted.value: Outflow catalog likely incomplete, especially low-velocity or near plane-of-sky outflows in crowded regions.
